glasses_policy.value: Prescription/corrective eyeglasses may not be worn during the photo session ("عدم استعمال النظارات الطبية أثناء التصوير")

accessories.value: Contact lenses may not be worn during the photo session ("عدم استعمال العدسات اللاصقة أثناء التصوير")

headwear_policy.value: White-coloured headscarves (hijab), in any shade of white, may not be worn during the photo session ("عدم ارتداء اللون الأبيض بدرجاته المختلفة بالنسبة للحجاب أثناء التصوير") -- implying religious headscarves are otherwise permitted, just not in white tones (which would blend with the white background)

glasses.en: Prescription (corrective) eyeglasses may not be worn during the photo session.
glasses.ko: 촬영 시 도수 안경(교정용 안경)을 착용해서는 안 된다.
glasses.ja: 撮影時に度付き眼鏡(矯正用眼鏡)を着用してはならない。

accessories.en: Contact lenses may not be worn during the photo session.
accessories.ko: 촬영 시 콘택트렌즈를 착용해서는 안 된다.
accessories.ja: 撮影時にコンタクトレンズを着用してはならない。

headwear.en: White-coloured headscarves (hijab), in any shade of white, may not be worn during the photo session.
headwear.ko: 촬영 시 흰색 계열(모든 명도의 흰색)의 히잡(머리가리개)을 착용해서는 안 된다.
headwear.ja: 撮影時に白系統(あらゆる濃淡の白)のヒジャブ(頭部を覆うスカーフ)を着用してはならない。

cross_verification.note_en: Two official sources from the Embassy of the State of Libya in Washington, D.C. (embassyoflibyadc.org, an official Libyan diplomatic mission) were directly fetched/read: (1) the /passports page, confirming '2 passport-sized photos' are required for a new/replacement passport; and (2) an Arabic-language PDF ('RequiredD.pdf', directly read via PDF extraction) titled roughly 'Documents required to issue a new passport', which lists 'عدد (2) صور حديثة خلفية بيضاء' (2 recent photos, white background) among the required documents, and separately lists photo-session conduct rules ('ملاحظات') that apply because passport photos are captured on-site at the embassy by appointment: no contact lenses, no prescription glasses, and no white-toned hijab during the sitting. The white background finding matches the DB's '흰색' value exactly (no conflict). No exact millimeter size, head-height ratio, or explicit facial-expression rule was found on either official document, so these remain unverified; third-party vendor claims of '40x60mm / 4x6cm, min head height 38mm' were seen in this research but could not be traced to any Libyan government or embassy source and are therefore excluded per the truth-gate rule rather than used to confirm or refute the DB's '4 x 6cm' value.
